On April 3, 2015, CNN Student News covered several international stories from Switzerland, Kenya, and the Pacific Ocean. The report also focused on California’s serious drought, which has forced many people and businesses to use less water. Additionally, the show discussed two religious holidays celebrated around the world and two topics related to U.S. National Parks. You can find the full transcript of the show on this page, as well as a way to sign up for the CNN Student News Roll Call.

Misao Okawa, who was recognized by Guinness World Records as the oldest person in the world, has died at the age of 117. She passed away on Wednesday morning in Osaka, Japan, according to Tadahi Uchimura, a local city official.

Okawa was born on March 5, 1898. She is survived by three children, four grandchildren, and six great-grandchildren. Her family used to run a kimono shop in Osaka. She had lived in a nursing home there since 1997.

Satoshi Yoshioka, who works at the nursing home, told CNN that Okawa had a gentle personality and loved to eat. Her favorite foods were sushi and udon noodles. He also noted that she ate a lot

Documents obtained by CNN show that when the Missouri National Guard prepared to go to Ferguson, Missouri, last year to help stop riots, they used strong military language. They called the protesters "enemy forces" and "adversaries." The Guard went to Ferguson to support police officers. However, many community leaders and civil rights activists accused the police of using too much force and making the tense situation worse. The protests happened sporadically from August until the end of the year.

On Tuesday, gunmen attacked the Somali education ministry in Mogadishu, the capital of Somalia. The attack started with a suicide car bombing, which killed at least 12 people and injured 16 others. After the explosion, five gunmen entered the two-story building and shot people inside.

Al-Shabaab, an Islamist militant group, claimed responsibility for the attack. A spokesman for the group, Abu Musab, said they were responsible. A government security official, Mohamed Yusuf, said the attack began when two suicide bombers drove their cars into the entrance of the building, which houses the Ministry of Education, Culture & Higher Education.

Gregory Margolin, now 87, has seen two wars. When he was 16, he fought for the Soviet Red Army against the Nazis in World War II. During that time, his family ran away. Margolin says he did not tell people he was Jewish, but it did not matter because everyone around him was being killed.

This year, at age 87, he found himself in another war in Ukraine. In the past, he was a sniper and became an army commander. He still has his old uniform with medals on it. His granddaughter, Liora, is amazed by his war stories and how he managed to survive.

It has been exactly one year since more than 200 Nigerian schoolgirls were taken from their dorms at night in Chibok, in northeastern Nigeria. They are still missing.

We should all feel ashamed that this happened. It is shameful that violent criminals can hurt young girls without facing consequences. It is also shameful that people stop paying attention so quickly after such terrible events occur.

In Norway, digital technology is replacing FM radio. The country plans to stop using FM radio completely within two years, making it the first nation to do so. This does not mean people will lose access to radio; they will just listen using digital signals instead. Government officials say that many of Norway’s 5 million people have already switched. While there are only five stations available on FM, there are four times as many on the Digital Audio Broadcasting network. According to Culture Minister Thorhild Widvey, half of the country now listens to radio digitally.

Everyone enjoys a good comeback story, especially one involving dinosaurs. A new study suggests that the Brontosaurus should have its own name again. For over 100 years, it was removed from science books, but researchers now believe it is distinct enough to be classified as its own type of dinosaur.

In 1879, O.C. Marsh named the Brontosaurus after receiving 25 crates of bones found at Como Bluff in Wyoming, according to the Yale Peabody Museum of Natural History. Marsh named it "Brontosaurus," which means "thunder lizard." He did this because the dinosaur was similar to, but not as large as, the Apatosaurus, which had been discovered a few years earlier.

Al Qaeda has joined a fight for control in Yemen by offering a reward. The group, known as Al Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula (AQAP), posted a news release and a wanted poster online. They are offering 20 kilograms of gold—worth about $774,000—to anyone who kills or captures two prominent Shia Muslim leaders. These leaders are Houthi rebel leader Abdelmalik Bedrudin Al-Houthi and former Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh. AQAP called them the "two heads of evil." This group is one of several factions fighting to take over Yemen.

Before landing his gyrocopter on the Capitol lawn on Wednesday, Doug Hughes explained his plans and reasons on a website called thedemocracyclub.org. The 61-year-old postal worker from Florida wrote in an online post titled "Your Pilot" that he wanted to highlight corruption in Washington, D.C., and offer solutions to it. He stated that his flight was not a secret. Before taking off, he sent an email to info@barackobama.com. In the message, he tried to convince Capitol security that he was not dangerous and that shooting him down would cause more trouble than allowing him to deliver letters to Congress.

Rio de Janeiro is facing more bad news before the 2016 Olympics. Many dead fish were found in the Rodrigo de Freitas lagoon. With just over a year left before the city hosts the rowing and canoe events, officials from Rio’s legislative assembly started an investigation on Monday. They are looking into why the fish died in the lagoon and in other lakes and bays across the state. This group will work together with the State Environmental Institute (INEA) and the State Secretariat for the Environment.

Anthony Ray Hinton is 58 years old, but he is just now learning how to live in the real world. He spent nearly 30 years on death row in Alabama, so simple things like using a fork, going out at night, or sleeping without someone watching him feel strange to him.

Last week, his murder convictions were canceled, and he was released from a county jail in Birmingham. He told CNN’s Brooke Baldwin that he has to remind himself that he is free. He said it will take some time to get used to his freedom.

For most of those 30 years, Hinton lived in a tiny cell that was only 5 feet by 7 feet.

According to opinion polls, there was no clear winner in the UK election debate featuring seven party leaders: David Cameron (Conservatives), Ed Miliband (Labour), Nick Clegg (Liberal Democrats), Nigel Farage (UK Independence Party), Natalie Bennett (Green Party), Nicola Sturgeon (Scottish National Party), and Leanne Wood (Plaid Cymru, the Welsh Nationalists).

Comres, which organized the debate for ITV, found that Cameron, Miliband, and Farage tied for first place with 21%, while Sturgeon was close behind with 20%. Meanwhile, ICM, which surveyed readers of The Guardian, ranked Miliband first with 25%, followed by Cameron with 24%, Farage with 19%, and Sturgeon with 17

A New York judge has ruled that Facebook is a valid way to serve divorce papers. This means a woman in Brooklyn can use the social media site to officially notify her husband of the divorce.

The woman, Ellanora Arthur Baidoo, has been trying to divorce her husband, Victor Sena Blood-Dzraku, for several years. Her lawyer, Andrew Spinnell, said they could not find Blood-Dzraku to hand him the legal documents.

According to court records, Baidoo has been able to call her husband. He told her that he does not have a permanent home or a job.

It sounds like a science fiction movie. A person has a terrible accident, ends up in the hospital, and is brain dead while on life support. Doctors usually ask families to donate organs to save up to eight people. But in this case, the family is asked to donate the entire head to save just one person. This might be for someone who is paralyzed from the neck down but has a sharp mind. Although this idea seems crazy, Italian doctor Sergio Canavero says we are close to making it happen. He calls the project HEAVEN, which stands for Head Anastomosis Venture. "Anastomosis" means surgically connecting two body parts.

Police say that Anthony Stokes’ life ended tragically on Tuesday, rather than with the happy ending his family had hoped for. Stokes, a teenager who had received a heart transplant, was involved in a series of crimes before his death. He stole a car, broke into a house, and shot at an elderly woman. He then led police on a high-speed chase and died after his car crashed into a pole.

In 2013, Stokes’ family told the media that an Atlanta hospital had refused to perform his heart transplant surgery. The hospital stated in a letter that they rejected him because of his "history of non-compliance," meaning he did not follow their medical instructions. At that time, Mark Bell was speaking to the press on behalf of the Stokes family.

At Garissa University College in Kenya, the sun had not yet risen on Thursday morning. Most students were still sleeping in their beds. A few had woken up early to attend Christian prayers.

The attack began around 5:30 a.m. (10:30 p.m. ET Wednesday) with an explosion and gunshots at the front gates. The attackers then moved through the campus, shooting as they went. The Red Cross reported that they stopped at a girls’ dormitory. At one point, they broke into a room where Christians had gathered and took people hostage, according to lecturer Joel Ayora.

Freddie Gray’s white casket was at the front of New Shiloh Baptist Church in West Baltimore. A gospel choir sang as a large crowd gathered to honor him. Gray, who was 25 years old, died in police custody 15 days after he was arrested for a weapons charge. He died from a serious spinal cord injury, which caused widespread anger toward the Baltimore Police Department. His death is the most recent in a series of high-profile cases involving African-Americans and law enforcement. Many people have demanded answers about what happened to Gray. His funeral was attended by civil rights leaders, politicians, and family members of other people who have died in police custody.

I have worked as a chef since I was 14, but I did not start fighting for food policy changes until much later. In 2007, I saw a young girl my wife was mentoring looking through the trash for food. This experience inspired me to start Food Policy Action and get involved in politics regarding food issues, such as hunger and factory farms. I have not worked alone on this. A major influence was "The Meatrix," a 2003 animated video made by the GRACE Communications Foundation. This video, which parodies the movie "The Matrix," clearly showed the health risks and environmental damage caused by factory farming.

Dan Swangard is a doctor who knows what death looks like. He has seen patients die in hospitals, often connected to pain medication and feeling very anxious. He has watched people suffer for weeks or months while their scared families stood by, unable to help. Recently, this topic has become personal for him. In 2013, he was diagnosed with a rare type of cancer that had spread. To treat it, surgeons removed parts of his pancreas and liver, as well as his entire spleen and gallbladder. The surgery worked, but Swangard, who is 48 years old, knows there is a high chance the cancer will come back.

A Saudi source told CNN that Saudi special forces helped Yemeni fighters fight against the Houthis and their allies in Aden. The special forces were on the ground but did not fight directly. Instead, they helped plan and guide the battle against Houthi forces and fighters who support former Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh. The special forces also helped drop weapons and communication equipment by parachute.

According to the source, Houthi rebels left the presidential palace and other important areas in Aden, a southern port city, after heavy airstrikes by Saudi planes. This move was a change from the previous day, when Houthi forces had taken control of the presidential palace.

A mother from Detroit, Mitchelle Angela Blair, was charged with murder and torture this week. Police found the bodies of her two children, 13-year-old Stoni Ann Blair and 9-year-old Stephen Gage Berry, inside a freezer last month.

The bodies were discovered on March 24 by a bailiff who was carrying out a court-ordered eviction. They were wrapped in plastic.

According to the medical examiner, Stoni died from multiple blunt force injuries, and Stephen died from both blunt force injuries and burns.

Wladimir Klitschko, the current world heavyweight boxing champion, has a major fight coming up, but he is mostly worried about the struggle for democracy in his home country, Ukraine. He spoke to CNN from his training center in Miami before his match with American boxer Bryant Jennings on April 25 in New York. Klitschko said the crisis in Ukraine has left him shocked and upset. He explained that his country is suffering because of the war with Russia. He clarified that Ukraine did not attack any other nation; instead, Russia is the one that attacked.

Michael Keaton hosted "Saturday Night Live" for the third time this weekend. He made small references to his roles in "Beetlejuice" and "Batman." In his opening speech, Keaton noted that much has changed since he first hosted the show in 1982. He mentioned that he has a 31-year-old son and a 28-year-old girlfriend. Fans who wanted to see him fully act out his famous characters were likely disappointed. Cast members Taran Killam and Bobby Moynihan sang a song asking him to play Batman and Beetlejuice. Keaton only responded with a few short jokes.

About a month ago, Kamron Taylor was found guilty of murder in an Illinois court. On Wednesday morning, he was in an Illinois jail. He hid outside his cell, waiting to attack. When a correctional officer came to check on him, Taylor beat up the guard. He then took the officer’s uniform and keys. Taylor walked out of the jail and got into the officer’s brown 2012 Chevrolet Equinox SUV. No one knows where the 23-year-old is now. He was supposed to be sentenced in May. The SUV was found around 8:30 a.m. (9:30 a.m. in another time zone).

A New York City detective, Ian Cyrus, has been suspended after being accused of stealing $3,000 during an illegal raid on cigarettes. Police spokesman Stephen Davis confirmed the suspension.

Video from a news station shows Detective Cyrus putting cash into a bag before leaving the Yemen Deli and Grocery store in Brooklyn last Friday. The police had arrested two employees for selling loose cigarettes.

The store’s manager, Ali Abdullah, noticed the money was missing from a box. He first thought one of his employees had taken it. However, after checking the security cameras, he was shocked by what he saw.

London (CNN) The Hatton Garden heist, which will likely be remembered by this name, was a terrible event for safe deposit box owners but a perfect scenario for a movie. Over the recent holiday weekend, thieves used heavy cutting tools and climbing gear to break into the vault of a well-known, 60-year-old safe deposit company in central London. They may have had up to four days to search through countless safe deposit boxes. Reports say they stole hundreds of thousands of pounds worth of jewelry and cash. One former police official estimates the total value could be as high as 200 million pounds, or about $300 million.

As we get closer to April 27, the day South Africa celebrates the first elections after apartheid in 1994, we are seeing another wave of deadly attacks against African migrants. People are expressing their anger about this violence on social media, using the hashtag "#WeAreAfrica" to show that everyone needs to stand together against these attacks. These repeated attacks on migrants and their belongings suggest that South Africa’s dream of being a "rainbow nation" is failing. That dream was about creating a country where people of all races and social classes could live with dignity.

In 1989, Ayatollah Khomeini said he was “drinking poison” when he agreed to a ceasefire to end the eight-year war with Iraq. The war had helped define his government, the Islamic Republic, which he had established one year before Saddam Hussein invaded Iran. Khomeini united the country, including both his supporters and his critics, to fight against the enemy. He kept the war going for eight years, even though Saddam was ready to stop fighting, which helped strengthen the Islamic Republic. By the time the war ended, the economy was ruined, and his most loyal volunteers were gone.

According to CNN, the concept of sustainable development suggests that unchecked capitalism is too strong for its own benefit. The global economy is growing rapidly, doubling in size every generation. However, because Earth has limited resources and the population is increasing by one billion people every 15 years, this rapid growth is damaging the natural environment and the social systems that support a good quality of life. Sustainable development provides a solution to this crisis. The article states that unchecked capitalism is essentially driven by greed.

The United States has benefited greatly from being a space-faring nation. Space access has helped protect U.S. national security, defense, and the economy. To fight current and future conflicts, combat terrorism, and handle growing global threats, the U.S. military relies on space-based tools like intelligence, GPS, and communications satellites. However, as global threats grow and the need for reliable space access increases, the U.S. faces a serious problem: it depends too much on Russian technology to meet its national security needs.

One year after nearly 300 schoolgirls were kidnapped by Boko Haram in Nigeria, Malala Yousafzai wrote an open letter to them on Monday. Malala is a 17-year-old who won the Nobel Peace Prize. She survived an attack by the Taliban in Pakistan because they did not want her to go to school or blog about education. In her letter, Malala says that she was also targeted by militants who did not want girls to attend school. She asks the Nigerian government and the rest of the world to do more to help rescue the missing girls. This letter was released shortly after Nigeria held an election.

On Tuesday evening, South African soldiers were sent to stop deadly violence against immigrants. This is part of a new plan by the government. The soldiers’ first goal was the neighborhood of Jeppestown in Johannesburg, where attacks on immigrants started on Friday.

While the soldiers guarded the area, police raided a hostel in Jeppestown. Earlier that day, Defense Minister Nosiviwe Mapisa-Nqakula announced the plan. She said an unknown number of soldiers would be sent to places where police are stretched too thin trying to stop the deadly attacks. She stated that this move does not mean the police are failing.

According to Iranian state media, eight Iranian border guards were killed in fighting with militants near the border with Pakistan. The clashes happened on Monday in Negur, a town in southeastern Iran. Iranian forces killed three of the militants during the fight.

The state news agency IRNA reported that Ali Asghar Mirshekari, the deputy governor of Iran’s Sistan-Baluchestan province, said the militants crossed into Iran from Pakistan. Iranian officials have asked Pakistani authorities to help catch the militants who survived the fighting.

According to CNN, TripAdvisor has named Providenciales in the Turks and Caicos as the number one island in the world. This is an improvement for Providenciales, which was ranked second last year. It moved up to take the top spot from Ambergris Caye, an island in Belize. Ambergris Caye had been the number one island for two years, but it fell out of the top ten this year. A TripAdvisor spokesperson, Julie Cassetina, said it is difficult to explain why rankings change each year because they depend on feedback from travelers.

The "Star Wars" story is growing with news about the 2016 movie "Rogue One." These details were shared at a fan event in Anaheim, California, on Sunday. Director Gareth Edwards showed a short preview clip and explained the plot. Disney calls this type of movie an "anthology" rather than a "spinoff." It stars Felicity Jones.

The story happens between two earlier films: "Episode III: Revenge of the Sith" and "Episode IV: A New Hope" (the original 1977 movie). In the film, a group of rebels goes on a secret mission to steal plans for the Death Star. Felicity Jones plays one of these rebel soldiers.

Tehran, Iran (CNN) There is a Persian saying: "A good year is determined by its spring." For many Iranians, the historic decision by Tehran and six world powers—the United States, Britain, France, Germany, Russia, and China—to keep talking about nuclear issues under a "joint comprehensive plan of action" means that this year’s Norouz, the Persian New Year that began on March 21, will be a great one. Even though some strict political opponents might try to cause trouble and complain that the early agreement isn’t exactly what they wanted, many people see it as excellent progress. That is what they hope for.

Ferguson, Missouri (CNN) [Updated at 11:45 p.m. ET] Two African-Americans, Ella Jones and Wesley Bell, were elected to the Ferguson City Council on Tuesday. This means that three of the six council members are now black.

[Original story, published at 6:52 p.m. ET] The weather was bad, with dark skies and radio warnings about possible flash floods. Despite the rain, the voting centers opened at 6 a.m. for local elections. Usually, very few people vote in these elections, but today was different. On Wednesday night, one person died and another was hurt in what police believe was a terror attack near Hebrew University in Jerusalem. According to Israel Police spokesman Micky Rosenfeld, a 37-year-old Arab man from East Jerusalem drove his car into two people who were standing at a bus stop in the French Hill area. One of the victims, Shalom Yohai Cherki, who was 26 years old, died in the hospital. The other victim, a 20-year-old woman, is still in serious condition. The driver has been arrested and is being investigated by the General Security Services.

Lauren Bacall, a famous actress who died in 2014, has put her large art collection up for sale. The collection features works by some of the most important artists of the 20th century. It was sold at an auction in New York on March 31. Before that, the art was shown to the public in Hong Kong, Paris, London, and Los Angeles.

Bacall became famous in 1944 with her first movie, "To Have And Have Not." She was 89 when she died in August 2014. It was during the filming of "To Have And Have Not" that she met her husband, Humphrey Bogart. She was known for her deep voice. At the 20

People in Kiev, Ukraine, are asking who is killing people who supported Ukraine’s former president, Viktor Yanukovych. This idea isn’t new, but it became a big concern this week because two important people were shot and killed in the city. One was a former lawmaker who had ties to Yanukovych, and the other was a journalist known for supporting Russia. The former lawmaker, Oleg Kalashnikov, was shot and killed shortly after 7 p.m. on Wednesday at the entrance to his apartment building.

Chile will soon recognize civil unions for same-sex couples. On Monday, President Michelle Bachelet signed a new law that allows these unions, joining several other South American countries. Bachelet said this is an important step toward treating gay and straight couples equally. The law will start in six months. It gives legal status to relationships between two people of the same sex, as well as to relationships between a man and a woman. The government estimates that about 2 million people will benefit from this change.

Next time you fly to Florida, sit by the window and look down at the Everglades as you land in Miami or Orlando. The area looks like a huge, muddy swamp filled with dangerous animals like snakes, scorpions, rats, roaches, alligators, and mosquitoes. In fact, one researcher once caught 365,000 bugs in just one trap in a single night. The Everglades show how mistakes made by people can be expensive to fix.

In early April, ISIS militants took over the Yarmouk Palestinian refugee camp, which is located near Damascus. For more than two years, the camp had been under attack and surrounded by Syrian forces. When the residents woke up, they faced a new and frightening situation: ISIS had defeated other armed groups in the area and seized control of almost the entire camp. One resident, who asked not to be named, told CNN that ISIS fighters killed people in the streets, including three men who were executed in front of others.

According to a study published on Friday, China’s internet censors are no longer satisfied with just using the "Great Firewall" to block citizens from reading Western news or other content they dislike. They have created a new tool called the "Great Cannon" and are using it to attack servers located outside China, including in the United States. The study’s authors note that this tool works openly and that launching such visible attacks inside other countries will likely anger the international community. They suggest that Beijing may have expected this reaction.

German prosecutors say that while investigators have not found any proof of why co-pilot Andreas Lubitz crashed Germanwings Flight 9525, medical records show he had suicidal thoughts and received therapy before he became a pilot. Spokesman Christoph Kumpa stated that no writings or conversations were found in which Lubitz explained his motives or admitted to any plans.

On Sunday, the leader of Yemen’s Houthi rebels said he would not give up. This statement came after a top Saudi military official claimed that weeks of airstrikes had significantly weakened the group.

Abdul-Malik al-Houthi, the rebel leader, said in a TV speech that his fighters would not leave the main cities or government buildings. He added that anyone thinking the rebels would surrender was wrong.

These comments followed more than three weeks of bombings by a Saudi-led coalition. The coalition’s goal is to push back the Houthis, who took over the capital, Sanaa, in January and removed President Abdu Rabu Mansour Hadi from power.

On April 19, 1995, twenty years ago, Timothy McVeigh blew up a large truck bomb outside the Murrah Federal Building in Oklahoma City. The attack killed 168 people, including men, women, and children, and hurt hundreds more. It is still the worst act of domestic terrorism in U.S. history.

The media covered the event heavily, using themes like "attack on the heartland" and America's "lost innocence." The bombing surprised the country. People were not just focused on how big the tragedy was, but on the fact that it showed something new: American citizens attacking their own government with deadly force never seen before.

If you cared deeply about something, would you protest? Would you make a sign or join a demonstration? How long could you keep trying when people ignored you or did nothing?

A year ago, more than 200 Nigerian girls were kidnapped from their school by Boko Haram militants. In response, millions of people around the world used social media to ask for their safe return. Charles Alasholuyi was one of these people, along with celebrities and world leaders. They expressed their anger using the hashtag #BringBackOurGirls. This was one of the most popular Twitter hashtags of 2014, appearing in more than four million tweets. However, as weeks turned into months, there was still no sign of the missing girls. Eventually, attention to the campaign faded.

Barney Frank, a retired former congressman, recently spoke to a full crowd in Chicago about his 45 years in politics. He was the first member of Congress to marry someone of the same sex while serving in office. During the talk, he criticized politicians who hide their sexual orientation but vote against LGBT rights. When a young man in the audience asked about a California ballot measure that would ban gay people, Frank said he did not know about the proposal. He told the young man not to worry about "crazy people."

A violent attack at Garissa University College in Kenya has killed nearly 150 people, including students, and injured dozens more. According to officials, gunmen stormed the campus early Thursday morning while people were attending morning prayers. They shot randomly and took hostages before security forces killed them. The U.S. Embassy in Nairobi stated that the militant group Al-Shabaab claimed responsibility for the attack. This tragedy happened just months after Al-Shabaab killed non-Muslim workers at a Kenyan quarry. The group has been responsible for many attacks in the area and has also recruited some Americans, especially Somali-Americans living in Minnesota.

A university in South Africa is celebrating the removal of a statue of a British colonial leader after weeks of protests. Students at the University of Cape Town used social media to demand that the statue of Cecil Rhodes be taken down, arguing that his history is marked by racism. They started a campaign last month using the hashtag #RhodesMustFall. Four weeks later, the campaign is now called #RhodesHasFallen. On Wednesday, the university announced that it received permission from heritage authorities to remove the statue from campus. The university stated that these steps are being taken to keep the statue safe while decisions about its future are being made.

Syria is becoming a terrible place, and the situation is getting worse. According to the Syrian Observatory for Human Rights, the number of people killed has doubled in just one year. They reported that 310,000 people have died since the civil war began. A year before that, the number was 162,402, and two years before that, the United Nations estimated 70,000 deaths. The UN says that more than half of all Syrians are so poor that they desperately need help to survive. Food rations are being reduced because there are not enough donations.

Ailina Tsarnaeva went into Manhattan Criminal Court quietly and seemed shy. However, prosecutors say she was not afraid to threaten someone she saw as a rival.

According to a criminal complaint, Tsarnaeva called a woman this summer and told her to stay away from her boyfriend. The complaint says Tsarnaeva told the woman, "Leave my man alone" and "Stop looking for him." She also said, "I know people that can put a bomb where you live."

Because of who Tsarnaeva is, prosecutors did not think the threats were a joke. They charged her with aggravated harassment, which she denies.

Police in Gaza took a door with a graffiti drawing by the British artist Banksy on Thursday after a disagreement about its sale. A police official in Gaza told CNN that the door’s owner, Rabea Darduna, went to court. He said he did not know how valuable the door was when he sold it for just $175. The police in Khan Younis, in southern Gaza, will keep the iron door until a court hearing date is set. Darduna says that when his home was destroyed in last summer’s war, he felt he had lost everything, except for the doorway and the door.

The attacks on Houthi rebels in Yemen continued on Tuesday. A Saudi-led group is taking more control of the area, while many locals are fleeing and dozens of civilians have been killed.

Five days after starting their air strikes, the coalition has destroyed the air defense systems of the Houthis and supporters of former Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh. They have also made almost all air bases and runways unusable, according to a source from Saudi Arabia.

Additionally, Saudi Arabia’s navy now controls all ports in Yemen. They are allowing only carefully monitored non-military medical supplies to pass through the blockade.

Holland’s coach, Guus Hiddink, strongly criticized his own fans for booing Spain’s player, Andres Iniesta, during Holland’s 2-0 win over Spain on Tuesday. He called the fans a “disgrace.”

Spain’s coach, Vicente del Bosque, used a new lineup for the match at the Amsterdam Arena. Iniesta started on the bench and came into the game in the 76th minute. When he did, the home fans shouted jeers and boos at him.

Holland’s Stefan de Vrij and Davy Klaassen scored goals in the first half, giving the team a morale boost. However, Hiddink was unhappy with how Iniesta was treated. The text also notes that Iniesta was playing for Spain during

Scotland will find out on May 21 whether its upcoming Euro 2016 soccer match against Georgia will be played without any fans in the stadium. UEFA, the sport’s governing body in Europe, has started an investigation into the Georgian Football Federation because fans ran onto the field twice during Georgia’s 2-0 loss to Germany on Sunday in Tbilisi. UEFA is also looking into claims that fans set off fireworks. Additionally, they are investigating several safety problems, such as blocked stairs, locked gates, and staff failing to search fans for weapons at the Boris Paichadze Stadium.

Football agents were waiting on Wednesday for news about new rules. Starting April 1, the system for licensing agents will change. Now, anyone can become a football agent if they pay £500 for their first year. After that, the FA will charge £250 each year to renew the license. Agents who already had licenses do not need to change anything. The FA plans to put a link on their website for agents to register, but as of 1pm, the link was not yet available. Mel Stein believes these new rules will cause chaos. These changes happen because FIFA has stopped regulating agents.

Maksims Uvarenko, the Latvian goalkeeper for CSKA Sofia, has not received his salary for three months since he joined the club in January. Because of this, he has had to ask his parents to send him money to pay his rent. Despite these financial troubles, Uvarenko, who signed an 18-month contract, says he is impressed by the club’s "unique" and passionate fans. He told local media on Wednesday, "The lack of money is the biggest problem I've faced at CSKA."

A court heard that David Moore, 25, attacked Rafal Cegielka, 45, because he was angry about traffic. Moore had just left his home and got stuck in heavy traffic next to Cegielka, who was picking up his child from St John's Primary School in Burnley, Lancashire. Moore punched Cegielka and then broke his car with a hockey stick in front of young children. Moore said he was having a bad day and lost his temper.

Spain lost 2-0 to Holland on Tuesday. This result brought back painful memories of Spain’s terrible performance in the 2014 World Cup. However, Gerard Pique says that coach Vicente del Bosque should not worry too much about this being Spain’s third straight loss in a friendly match.

Holland had previously beaten Spain 5-1 during the group stage of the 2014 World Cup in Brazil. That loss ended Spain’s six-year reign as the top team in world soccer. In this recent match, Holland scored two goals early in the game at the Amsterdam Arena. They then held off strong pressure from Spain in the second half to win 2-0.

Police say a New York City mother, Ulrike Berger, 44, has taken her seven-year-old daughter, Kaia, to Germany during a custody dispute. A court order forbids Berger from leaving the United States with the child. However, police believe the pair flew from New York to Germany on March 22. This happened just one day after Kaia’s father dropped her off for a weekend visit at Berger’s home in Boerum Hill, Brooklyn, at 10 a.m. on March 21. Police are now searching for them.

A large fire burned through dry heathland near the south coast of Britain. The fire created big flames and thick, bad-smelling smoke. It destroyed an area the size of 100 football fields, looking like a scene from a disaster movie. This happened after days of storms hit Britain, which knocked down trees and closed roads. The 70-hectare area in Dorset was very dry because it is on a hillside, so rainwater ran off the slope. Fire investigators confirmed that the fire was started on purpose. Three separate areas of heath were destroyed: one was half a hectare, another was one hectare, and the largest was 70 hectares.

Last night, emergency services in Britain received 600 calls every hour as people celebrated the New Year in 2012. Paramedics were overwhelmed, and in Cambridge, a military field hospital was opened to help drunk partygoers. The London Ambulance Service said that at the busiest time, they handled more than 600 calls per hour—more than three times the usual number. In Manchester, one man collapsed on the sidewalk next to an ambulance while two people walked by eating late-night food. In another part of Manchester, a man was slumped in a doorway while two women walked past during their New Year celebrations.

Liverpool goalkeeper Simon Mignolet says his mental strength helped him bounce back after being dropped from the team last December. Manager Brendan Rodgers removed him "indefinitely" because of poor performance, but Mignolet returned quickly when backup goalkeeper Brad Jones hurt his thigh. The 27-year-old Belgian player explained that he stayed positive despite being upset about being cut from the squad. Mignolet told FourFourTwo magazine, "I was positive."

On Tuesday, large hailstones, about the size of plums, fell across the Southern United States. Many people went outside to film the unusual weather.

Arke USA, a Twitter user from Bryant, Arkansas, recorded video of the ice balls hitting his backyard and splashing loudly into his swimming pool. The footage shows the hailstones falling quickly. Many broke when they hit the ground.

Even though the temperature was around 80 degrees, the hard ice did not melt right away. Within seconds, the patio was covered in white hail.

Nine people from the *Liana’s Ransom*, a replica pirate ship, had to leave their boat because it lost power in rough seas off the coast of Maine. The ship is from Canada. Coast Guard officials said the crew was rescued on Tuesday by lifeboats, leaving the ship drifting 30 miles east of Portland. The crew reported engine problems around 12:35 a.m. on Monday and said the sails got tangled around the mast. The Coast Guard helped the crew members jump from the ship to safety.

Stunning photos show blue glowing algae lighting up Australia’s east coast. The pictures were taken in Jervis Bay, on the south coast of New South Wales, showing the bright glow on one of Australia’s popular beaches. Photographer Andy Hutchinson called the sight a “beautiful supernatural scene” caused by millions of tiny plankton that emit light. A similar event happened at Sydney’s Manly Beach in August 2014. At that time, an oceanography expert told Daily Mail Australia that people did not need to worry about the algae.

A 17-year-old boy named Rahul Kumar was rescued by zoo security after he jumped into a lion enclosure at the Kamla Nehru Zoological Park in Ahmedabad, India. Kumar climbed over the fence and ran toward the lions, shouting that he was going to kill them. He later explained that he was drunk and believed he had a good chance of winning against the animals. Security staff were surprised when he suddenly ran toward the lions while sitting nearby.

A 12-year-old boy in Nanchang, China, survived after falling from a fifth-story window. He landed on a car parked below, which saved his life. His father said the boy was likely sleepwalking when he fell. The accident happened last Saturday night. A hotel receptionist across the street heard a loud crash around midnight and thought it was a car accident.

Drew Miller, a player for the Red Wings, is excited to play again just one day after getting a serious cut on his face. He said he feels very lucky that a skate did not hit his eye. During practice on Wednesday, he wore a full face mask and showed a large, bloody wound that needed 50 to 60 stitches to close. Although he has a scar across his eye, reports say his eyesight was not damaged.

Filipe Luis says he wants to stay at Chelsea until his contract ends, even though Atletico Madrid might try to sign him again this summer. He joined Chelsea from Atletico last July with a three-year deal, but he has had trouble playing well as their left back. Atletico thinks this might help them get him back, but Luis says, “I am happy at Chelsea. I want to stay at the club until my contract is over.”

Charlie Sumner, a 20-year-old fan of Reading Football Club, is facing a three-year ban from stadiums. Last month, he attended his first-ever game at the Madejski Stadium. During the FA Cup quarter-final replay, where Reading won 3-0 against Bradford City, Sumner ran onto the field while his team was leading 3-0. He performed four front flips, landing on his back, before being stopped by security staff. Sumner, who described attending his first game as a "brilliant experience," now faces the potential three-year ban for this stunt.

A scary video shows a group of men riding on top of a van being thrown off when the vehicle swerved around a corner. About six people were sitting on the roof of the van on a road near Salé, a city in Morocco. The van was driving fast and tipped over onto its side. The footage was recorded by a car following the van, which is believed to be carrying football fans. The video shows the crowded van moving back and forth on a busy road with two lanes.

England is in Group D of the UEFA Under-17 European Championships, along with the Republic of Ireland, Holland, and Italy. The tournament will be held in Bulgaria in May.

England’s coach, John Peacock, leads the team, known as the Young Lions. They are the current champions because they beat Holland in last year’s final in Malta. To move forward to the quarter-finals, England must beat Holland again. This year’s tournament is bigger than before, with 16 teams instead of eight.

Also, Danny Collinge scored his first goal for England against Norway during the qualifying matches.

An elephant in South Africa’s Kruger National Park was relaxing by a small pool of water with its family when a male buffalo came too close. The elephant was annoyed by the buffalo’s presence. It tried to spray water from its trunk to make the buffalo leave, but it missed. The video shows the frustrated elephant trying again while its young calf stays close to its parent for protection.

Michael Thorpe, a former pub owner, has won an eight-year legal battle to clear his name. He was originally convicted in November 2006 for showing Premier League football matches on foreign TV channels at his pub, the Stoke Inn in Plymouth, Devon. At the time, he did not have permission from the official broadcasters. The court has now overturned his conviction. However, Thorpe says the long fight has been very costly, and he has lost his pub as a result.

The Irish Football Association hopes that structural damage at Windsor Park in Belfast will not stop the team from playing their important Euro 2016 match against Romania in June. Cracks were found in the West Stand on Tuesday morning, so the area was closed off while engineers checked the damage. A spokesperson said the association learned about the damage, which happened overnight on Monday night, on Tuesday morning.

Charlie Sumner, 20, is facing a three-year ban from football stadiums. The ban comes after he ran onto the field topless and did four front flips during his first game at the stadium.

The incident happened last month at Reading's Madejski Stadium during an FA Cup match against Bradford City. Sumner, a fan of Reading, performed the stunt while his team was winning 3-0. He landed on his back after each flip before being stopped by security guards.

A BMW driver was arrested today after hitting and killing Hina Shamim, a talented student, as she walked to the library. Hina, 21, died near the University of Kingston in London last night, just weeks before her 22nd birthday. There were five children in the car with the driver.

Friends have left flowers at the scene to remember Hina. They said she was originally from Peterborough, had the nickname "Hyena," and was a much-loved, charming, and lovely girl.

A mother and her teenage daughter were arrested after a video of them fighting with a high school student went online. The incident happened at Langham Creek High School in Houston on Tuesday. According to Channel 2, the mother was angry because the student had allegedly been bullying her daughter. The mother’s name has not been released. In the video, the mother is wearing a black top on the right, and the student she was fighting with is in the center wearing white.

Stoke’s boss, Tony Scholes, hopes to keep Asmir Begovic as their goalkeeper. Begovic is in the last year of his contract. He is 27 years old and has been linked with other clubs while playing at the Britannia Stadium. Even though his contract has just over 12 months left, Scholes thinks they can match the player’s goals.

Scholes told The Sentinel, “Clearly Asmir is a great goalkeeper and we really want him to stay at the club.” He added, “When you have very good players, it is natural that people talk about where they will go next.”

A bus driver in Auckland, New Zealand, was fired by his boss for reading a newspaper while driving. A passenger recorded the incident on video and sent it to the bus company, Ritchies Coachlines, along with a complaint. The video shows the driver turning pages while the bus is moving. When the bus stops at traffic lights, the driver looks closely at one of the pages. The boss of Ritchies Coachlines, Andrew Ritchie, said he was embarrassed by the driver’s behavior and called him an idiot.

West Ham manager Sam Allardyce says that defender Winston Reid will be ready to play in Saturday’s game against Leicester City, who are currently at the bottom of the league. However, Enner Valencia will not be able to play.

Reid had been injured since March 4, when he hurt his hamstring in a 1-0 loss to Chelsea. But during the break for international matches, he returned to full training.

Valencia missed West Ham’s last two games against Arsenal and Sunderland because of an unusual toe injury he suffered in mid-March. Allardyce says Valencia is still not fit enough to play.

Allardyce confirmed, “We’ve got Winston back in full training.”

Five days before their wedding last May, college sweethearts Brittany Huber and John Redman were in a terrible car accident on a highway in Georgia. The crash killed Brittany, who was the bride, and left John, the fiancé, fighting for his life.

John survived, but his body was badly injured. Doctors told him he would probably spend the rest of his life in a nursing home and use a wheelchair. At 25, John was an assistant basketball coach at Dalton State College, and his future looked very difficult.

However, against all expectations, John recovered. On March 24, he helped lead his team to win a championship title.

Lucas (on the left) and Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard played together in a charity All-Star game at Anfield on Sunday. Lucas, a midfielder from Brazil, wants to get back to his best form after recovering from an injury.

From late November until February, he started 16 out of 19 games. During this time, the team’s results improved significantly. However, he hurt his groin in a match against Everton in February and missed 10 games.

He did not play in the loss to Manchester United, which was Liverpool’s first league defeat since mid-December. But he played the full 90 minutes in Sunday’s charity game at Anfield.

Do you find father-daughter photos boring? Japanese photographer Yûki Aoyama has found a funny way to make them more interesting. In his new book, which is called *Daughter and Salary Man*, he shows serious-looking teenage daughters standing next to their fathers who are jumping in the air. In every picture, the daughter looks at the camera and smiles, while her father strikes a dramatic pose. Aoyama is 37 years old.

Police are looking for a man aged between 50 and 60 who robbed a bank in Fairwater, Cardiff, at 12:30 pm. He took £3,000 in cash and ran away. The robbery happened at a Lloyds Bank branch.

Police have released CCTV photos of the suspect. He is a white man, between 5ft 9in and 6ft tall, with greying black hair and glasses. He was wearing black clothes. No one was hurt during the robbery. Police are confident that members of the public can help identify him.

The Court of Arbitration for Sport has removed Morocco’s ban from the next two African Cup of Nations tournaments. Previously, the Confederation of African Football (CAF) had kicked Morocco out of the 2017 and 2019 events and fined them $1 million. The CAF also asked for an additional $9 million in compensation because Morocco withdrew as hosts due to fears about the Ebola epidemic. The tournament was eventually won by Ivory Coast, who hosted it in Equatorial Guinea. Now, Morocco is allowed to take part in the next two editions of the competition.

Tom Boyd thinks Jason Denayer’s time on loan at Celtic has been so successful that he is now ready to try for a spot at Manchester City next season. This would mean Celtic manager Ronny Deila cannot keep Denayer for another year, as he had hoped. However, Boyd sees a good side to this. He believes Denayer’s success will show other young players that joining Celtic is a great way to grow their careers. The 19-year-old defender has done well at Celtic this season. He also recently earned his first game for the Belgium national team in a match against Cyprus.

Andros Townsend proved his critics wrong with a great goal for England. He said that negative comments from people like Paul Merson actually motivated him while he was in Italy.

This has been a confusing season for the 23-year-old, who has not played as well as he did when he first started playing for the national team. However, England’s manager, Roy Hodgson, still believed in him. Townsend showed his value with an excellent goal at Juventus Stadium.

He scored England’s equalizing goal in a 1-1 friendly match against Italy in Turin on Tuesday night. After scoring, Townsend celebrated with his Tottenham teammates, Ryan Mason and Kyle Walker.

Chinese company Dalian Wanda Group has officially bought a 20% stake in Spanish soccer team Atletico Madrid. The deal was finalized on Tuesday at an Extraordinary General Meeting. Wanda’s legal team signed papers to buy 726,707 shares for €45 million (£32.8 million). Although the purchase was first announced in January, two special meetings were required to approve it. Wanda’s chairman, Wang Jianlin, wants to increase Atletico’s popularity in Asia. The paragraph also mentions that Atletico’s manager, Diego Simeone, speaks to the media.

Antonio Conte said he had happy memories when he returned to Turin for Italy’s 1-1 tie with England. This was true even though reports said he received death threats before the friendly match.

Conte became the manager of the Italian national team in August, replacing Cesare Prandelli. This happened after Italy was eliminated in the group stage of last summer’s World Cup. However, his first seven months as coach have been very difficult and confusing.

Recently, Italy played against Bulgaria. The game ended in a 2-2 draw because Italy scored a late goal by Eder. Before that match, which was part of the Euro 2016 qualifiers, Juventus fans reportedly sent death threats to Conte. This happened after their player, Claudio Marchisio, injured his knee

Ian Murray thinks that Hibernian could overtake Rangers for second place in the Scottish Championship during the final month of the season. He believes Rangers will find it hard to keep up their current speed.

Murray’s team, Dumbarton, has already played against both Rangers and Hibernian this season, and they will face them again in the coming weeks. Even though Rangers are currently doing well—having beaten Hibernian and Cowdenbeath, while Hibernian lost to Raith—Murray does not think this situation will last. He expects the advantage to shift back to Hibernian soon.

Liverpool goalkeeper Simon Mignolet took photos with pilots in an airplane cockpit as he flew back to England. He had just finished playing for Belgium in Euro 2016 qualifying matches against Cyprus and Israel. Even though Mignolet was named in the team for both games, he did not play. Instead, Chelsea goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois was chosen. This meant Mignolet did not get to add to his 14 total games for his country. Mignolet shared the photos on his official Facebook account on Wednesday.

Chyknell Hall Estate is for sale for £6 million. It is a large rural property near Bridgnorth, Shropshire, covering 200 acres. The estate includes a Grade II-listed manor house, five cottages, a swimming pool, a tennis court, stables, and a cricket green. The main house, Chyknell Hall, has 11 bedrooms and was built in 1814. It has only been sold twice since it was built. Because the grounds are private and secluded, it may appeal to famous buyers.

Two college police officers in Dallas have been put on leave without pay after a video showed them harassing four students and arresting one of them. The video shows that the officers hit the student before arresting him.

The incident happened last Wednesday at El Centro College, a school in downtown Dallas. A student named Charles Adams recorded the event on his phone. Adams was standing outside the campus, waiting for a bus and smoking a cigarette, when he saw the officers approach the group of high school students.

Gary Locke has been named the permanent manager of Kilmarnock after signing a three-year contract. He originally joined the club last summer as assistant manager to Allan Johnston. However, when Johnston left in early February, Locke took over as head coach. Since then, the 39-year-old has led the team to six wins and only one loss in seven games. He will speak to the press on Friday morning. The photo shows Locke shaking hands with chairman Jim Mann after finalizing his new deal.

This weekend, one of the most important matches in German football is taking place. It is called "Der Klassiker," but it is not as exciting as it used to be. Borussia Dortmund and Bayern Munich have won the last five league titles together, and Bayern is likely to win again this season.

Even though these two teams are far apart in the standings—Bayern has 31 more points and is nine places higher than Dortmund—the match is still very important. The two teams are rivals in German football. The text also mentions that Jurgen Klopp, who was in the center, celebrated with his Borussia Dortmund players after they beat Hannover.

A 14-year-old schoolgirl named Deva Joseph was left crying at London Stansted Airport because easyJet would not let her board her flight to Spain. The airline said this was because she had two pieces of hand luggage. Deva offered to pay extra to put the second bag in the cargo hold, but she was told she could only pay by credit card. Since she is too young to have a credit card, she could not pay the fee.

Gordon Robson, 26, killed John Potts, 45, with one punch to the back of the head. The hit was so hard it made a loud cracking sound, and Mr. Potts fell down and died.

Robson was drunk after attending his grandfather’s funeral. He had stepped in to stop a fight outside the NE38 Sports Bar in Washington, Tyne and Wear, in November last year, when he hit Mr. Potts. Mr. Potts was a devoted father.

Robson has a history of violent crimes. He was sentenced to three and a half years in prison for this attack.

Scoring a goal against your former team and making a perfect set-piece happen are two of the best feelings in football. For Notts County player Ellen White, Thursday night was special because she did both at once against Arsenal in the Women's Super League.

In the 26th minute, Notts County was given a free kick near the penalty area. Her teammates, Laura Bassett and Alex Greenwood, got confused. They almost ran into each other, which caused a mix-up. Ellen White took advantage of this. She spun around near the edge of the box and kicked the ball into the corner, scoring against her old club.

High school girls in China are practicing military-style knife drills. They shout commands like "kill, stab, slash, and jab" while performing eight specific movements. The training takes place at Huizhou Integrated High School on March 27. Former special forces soldier Inspector Tan is teaching the 68 students, who are between 16 and 18 years old. For safety reasons, the knives they use are not real. School official Huang Anruo confirmed that the daggers are fake.

We spend one-third of our lives sleeping, but many of us ignore what our bodies and minds need to feel rested. A study by the Sleep Health Foundation shows that 30% of Australians complain about not getting enough sleep every day. Professor David Hillman says that if we miss out on sleep, we have to make up for it later to stay functional throughout the week. On average, adults need about eight hours of sleep each night, though anywhere from seven to nine hours is normal.

Video has been posted online showing a fight between neighbors in Perth, Australia. The video, which was shared on Facebook, shows an angry woman shouting racist insults at a group of men who appear to be African. She is standing over her fence.

Later, the woman is seen in her neighbor’s front yard holding a metal crowbar. She yells at the men and swings the crowbar at them. The men then grab their own weapons, and a fight breaks out.

In the video, the woman can be heard saying, “I don’t deal with monkeys. Go on, you f*****g monkeys.”

Manchester City, Arsenal, and Chelsea are all trying to sign 19-year-old Valencia defender Jose Luis Gaya this summer. They want to take him away from Real Madrid.

Pete Jenson from Sportsmail explains why English clubs are interested. Gaya has a buy-out clause of £13.5 million. This is a good deal because Luke Shaw, who is about the same age and has similar potential, cost £27 million. However, some people worry that Gaya might not be good enough for the Premier League. The text also notes that Gaya played for Valencia against Sevilla earlier this season.

Police in Oregon are asking the public for help to identify a motorcyclist who helped save two teenagers. The incident happened in Salem when a 59-year-old man named Edward West allegedly pointed a gun at the teens and told them, "get ready to die."

Just then, a stranger on a green motorcycle arrived. He used his helmet to knock the gun out of West’s hands, which allowed the teenagers to escape. The police are now looking for this mystery motorcyclist.

Tim Sherwood has told Aston Villa captain Ron Vlaar that he needs to prove himself again as he gets ready to return to the team. Sherwood wants the healthy defender to help the struggling club finish the season strongly. He also warned Vlaar that people might have forgotten his great performance at the World Cup last year.

Vlaar played well for Holland as they reached the semi-finals in Brazil. Even though he missed a penalty in the shootout against Argentina, his performance led to interest from Manchester United. Now, the strong Dutch defender is returning from injury to help Aston Villa fight against being relegated. He will play when the team visits Old Trafford on Saturday.

Aston Villa manager Tim Sherwood says he is not worried about the club being sold this summer. He wants to build a team that fits his style for next season, as long as the team avoids being relegated. The current owner, Randy Lerner, is talking in detail with a potential buyer. If someone else buys the club, people might wonder if Sherwood will keep his job. However, Sherwood is focused only on keeping the team in the league right now. He plans to make long-term changes during the summer break. This comes after a recent win where Aston Villa beat Sunderland, with Christian Benteke scoring a goal.

It is well known that Celtic wants to borrow Jason Denayer from Manchester City again next season. However, this might not happen. On Thursday, Manchester City’s manager, Manuel Pellegrini, said that his young players from the academy are not yet ready to play for the main team. Because of this, players like Denayer may have to return from their loans to help fill the squad. This is surprising because Denayer has done a good job while playing for Celtic on loan this season.

Southampton manager Ronald Koeman is waiting to find out exactly when Fraser Forster will be back before deciding if he needs to sign another goalkeeper this summer. Forster had knee surgery after falling badly during a 2-0 win against Burnley two weeks ago. Doctors say he could take anywhere from four to twelve months to recover. Koeman does not want to give a specific date for Forster’s return. He believes Kelvin Davis is a good backup player, but admits he might have to find another goalkeeper if Forster’s recovery takes too long.

Rotherham’s manager, Steve Evans, was very angry after his team lost a close match against Birmingham in the Sky Bet Championship. Rotherham was in danger of being relegated from the league.

Birmingham won the game with two goals in the first half, scored by Robert Tesche and Clayton Donaldson. Rotherham’s Matt Derbyshire scored one goal to make it closer, but Birmingham held on for the win.

About an hour into the game, Birmingham’s Rob Kiernan handled the ball clumsily while trying to stop Derbyshire. Derbyshire fell down inside the penalty area, and Rotherham asked the referee, Dean Whitestone, to award them a penalty kick. The referee refused, which made Evans even angrier. Virgil van Dijk is clearly worried. The Netherlands national team has already let in more goals in five Euro 2016 qualifying matches than they did in their entire qualifying campaign for the last World Cup. Despite this, national team coach Guus Hiddink has not contacted him. Van Dijk was selected for two squads last year, but his progress has been inconsistent. Recently, while the Dutch team was tied 1-1 with Turkey, Van Dijk was relaxing in the Arabian Gulf with his club teammates at Celtic. Even though he has been playing very well for Celtic, he has not been called up to the Netherlands national team.

Celtic are angry with the Scottish Football Association (SFA) about the ticket prices for their upcoming Scottish Cup semi-final against Inverness at Hampden. The match is scheduled for 12:15 pm on Sunday, April 18. This time has already upset Inverness fans because it is before the first trains from Inverness arrive in Glasgow.

Celtic has now complained about the prices, which are set at £23 for the North and South stands. Tickets are £15 for adults in the East Stand and £5 for concessions (such as children or seniors) in that same stand.

Paul Murray, the interim chairman of Rangers, said on Thursday night that the previous management teams are entirely responsible for the club being removed from the stock exchange. The club, based at Ibrox, must be delisted from the Alternative Investment Market (AIM) because it could not find a new advisor required by the rules. Murray stated that these changes will not affect the new board’s future plans or their intended investments.

Wayne Rooney and his England teammates were unhappy with how poorly they played at the start of their match against Italy on Tuesday night. This game was a friendly match held at the Juventus Stadium in Turin, just nine months after the two teams met at the World Cup. Even though England had won their last seven games in a row, they had a hard time in the first half. They deservedly lost the first half when Italy’s Graziano Pelle scored with a header. The match ended in a 1-1 tie. Afterward, England captain Wayne Rooney said that he and his teammates were upset by their performance in the first half.

Dundee United’s board has responded to strong criticism from two major supporters’ groups, Arabtrust and the Federation of Dundee United Supporters Clubs. These groups are shocked to learn that 25% of the £6.3 million paid for players Ryan Gauld, Andrew Robertson, Stuart Armstrong, and Gary Mackay-Steven went as commissions to unnamed people. The supporters’ groups also disagree with chairman Stephen Thompson’s claims about how much money he has invested in the club. In response, the board has defended itself by pointing to the team’s success on the field.

Gary Locke will officially become the permanent manager of Kilmarnock on Friday. This happens exactly eight weeks after he was first asked to manage the team until the end of the season. The club, which plays at Rugby Park, will make the announcement on Friday morning. Locke, who is 39 years old and previously managed Hearts, will sign a three-year contract. On Thursday, he thanked the players for their hard work, which helped him win the support of the new chairman, Jim Mann. Locke took over as caretaker manager in February after replacing Allan Johnston.

Chinese parents are very focused on raising children who are exceptionally talented, whether they are ten-year-olds entering university or four-year-olds who can dance like Michael Jackson. Now, a new basketball star is emerging. A video has gone viral in China, showing a young boy with impressive basketball skills that rival many professional players. According to People's Daily Online, the five-year-old boy, named Mai Zizhuo, has been playing basketball since he was two and a half. The video shows him making several baskets and then dribbling two basketballs at the same time while running.

Bayern Munich will miss versatile left-back David Alaba for the end of the season because he has a torn knee ligament and will be out for about seven weeks. Alaba was already out for three months earlier this year due to a partial tear in his right knee. He got hurt while playing for Austria in a 1-1 tie against Bosnia on Tuesday. The 22-year-old told the club’s website, “I am very disappointed. But I have a big goal, which is to be ready for the final match of the season.” The injury happened when Alaba was tackled by Emir Spahic during Austria’s 1-1 draw against Bosnia-Herzegovina.

Hull KR have signed experienced Australian player Dane Tilse from the Canberra Raiders to replace Michael Weyman and Ryan Bailey, who left the team. Tilse, 30, is 6ft 7in and weighs over 17 stone. He has signed a two-and-a-half-year deal with Hull KR and will join the team as soon as the paperwork is finished. The Raiders have agreed to let him go. Tilse has played 200 games in Australia. He will work with his former teammate Terry Campese, who is now Hull KR’s captain and recently signed a two-year contract extension. Tilse is a direct replacement for Weyman, who retired last month because of an injury.

Livingston’s manager, Mark Burchill, says that midfielder Darren Cole wants to play in Sunday’s Petrofac Cup final, even though the match is just one week after the tragic death of his cousin in America.

Darren Cole, who used to play for Rangers’ youth team, is grieving the loss of his cousin, 22-year-old Shaun Cole. Shaun was found dead on a street in Miami last weekend and is believed to have been hit by a car that fled the scene.

Shaun was a soldier who had served in Afghanistan. He was on leave and visiting Florida when he went to a music festival. Afterward, he was found on the sidewalk with a head injury, which turned out to be fatal.
